method: candidate-glyph grid + per-measure staff strips, adjudicated visually from the raster only
caveat: Single-reader visual tally with no second reader and no pixel-level verification, so counts are SCREENING estimates with roughly +/-4 tiles of uncertainty, not certified truth. Recall was judged qualitatively from strips and is NOT quantified.
false_negative_observation: Staff strips show unmarked noteheads, concentrated in dense beamed runs and in stacked chords, where several noteheads merge into one component or fall outside the height window. Recall NOT quantified.
mechanism_identified: O3 staff-line suppression removes long horizontal runs, which FRAGMENTS any glyph spanning the staff height. A treble clef, a time signature and several accidentals all span multiple lines, so each breaks into 2-5 fragments whose bounding boxes land inside the notehead width/height/fill window. One clef therefore yields several false candidates.
note: This is a mechanism-level finding, not a threshold problem: no choice of W_MIN/H_MAX/FILL_MIN removes a fragmented clef without also removing real noteheads, because the fragments genuinely have notehead-sized bounding boxes.
